questions: Did you suddenly lose strength or movement in your right arm or hand?
Did this problem begin after an injury to your neck, shoulder, or arm?
Do you have numbness or tingling in the affected arm or hand?
Do you have facial drooping, speech difficulty, vision loss, or weakness in either leg?
Did you lose consciousness or become confused when the symptoms began?
Have you had a similar episode before?
Does the arm move or become stiff without you intending it to?
Do the symptoms improve when you are distracted?
Do the symptoms worsen when someone watches or examines you?
Are you experiencing significant pain in the arm, neck, or chest?
Do you have diabetes, epilepsy, or a previous stroke?
Have you recently experienced unusual stress, anxiety, or emotional trauma?
orders: Comprehensive neurological examination with assessment of strength, tone, reflexes, sensation, coordination, gait, and abnormal movements during distraction, suggestion, entrainment, and voluntary movement
Video-EEG monitoring with surface EMG electrodes on the affected arm
Brain MRI with and without gadolinium
Cervical-spine MRI with and without gadolinium
Routine laboratory tests including CBC, electrolytes, glucose, calcium, magnesium, renal and liver function, thyroid function, vitamin B12, and toxicology screen
Nerve-conduction studies and needle EMG of both upper limbs
